title: 01 Baseline — all raw features
summary: All raw categorical + continuous columns, no feature selection, no mined patterns (2020 data)
notes:
## Setup

- Data: `Flight_tab_2020.csv` / `data_info_2020.yaml`, target `|ARR_DELAY| > 15 min`
- Temporal split by day-of-month: train `FL_DAY <= 9`, val `10-12`, test `> 12` (never shuffled across days)
- Excluded: `FLIGHTS`, `FL_YEAR`, `FL_MONTH`
- Two-phase training: phase 1 `RandomizedSearchCV` (n_iter 10, cv 3) on 10% of train over `d_model ∈ {64,128,256}`, `n_layers ∈ {2,6,10}`, `lr ∈ {1e-5,1e-4,1e-3}`; phase 2 retrain on **100% of train** (`phase2_frac: 1.0`), batch 4096, patience 3, GPU `16-mixed`

```bash
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/ablations/01_baseline_all_features/run.py
```

## Results

| Model | AUC | ACC |
|---|---|---|
| MLP | 0.5527 | 0.5891 |
| AutoInt | **0.5826** | **0.6045** |
| ResNet | 0.5365 | 0.5862 |
| FTTransformer | 0.5552 | 0.5886 |

**Finding:** the reference point. AUC ~0.54–0.58 across four deep tabular models — the ~19 features are only moderately predictive of a near-balanced target. AutoInt is the strongest architecture and stays strongest in almost every downstream arm.

⚠️ **Confound to keep in mind:** this arm alone trains phase 2 on the full training set (`phase2_frac: 1.0`, batch 4096); every child arm uses `phase2_frac: 0.1`, `val_frac: 0.1`, batch 2048, patience 5. Cross-arm AUC gaps therefore mix feature-set effect with training-budget effect.

children.title: 02 SHAP-only — top-10 SHAP features
children.summary: Keep only the 10 highest mean-|SHAP| features; isolates SHAP selection from HUIM patterns
children.notes:
## Setup

- `features.mode: shap_only`, `top_shap_n: 10`, ranking read from `../../SHAP_HUIM/shap_feature_importance.csv`
- Training matched to arms 03/04/06: `phase1_frac 0.1`, `phase2_frac 0.1`, `val_frac 0.1`, batch 2048, patience 5

```bash
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/ablations/02_shap_only/run.py
```

**Status:** config + `run.py` exist but the arm has **never been run** — no `results.csv` in the directory, and the hand-off dir `exp/Tab_exp/SHAP_HUIM/` it points at does not exist on disk (the extraction writes to `shap_huim_extractions/01_2024_baseline/csvs/`, and its outputs must be copied/renamed into `SHAP_HUIM/` first).

**Gap this leaves:** without it, the 03 (SHAP+HUIM) gain cannot be attributed between *SHAP selection* and *HUIM patterns* — 03 is currently only comparable to the full-feature baseline. This is the single most valuable missing run.

children.title: 03 SHAP + HUIM (proposed method)
children.summary: Top-10 SHAP features plus 20 delay-driver and 20 delay-protector HUIM patterns as binary columns
children.notes:
## Setup

- `features.mode: shap_plus_huim`, `top_shap_n: 10`, `top_drivers_n: 20`, `top_protectors_n: 20`, `n_bins: 5` (KBinsDiscretizer quantile bins for matching continuous items)
- Patterns come from the **2024** extraction; the model trains/evaluates on **2020** — the two years are deliberately not conflated (patterns are treated as year-independent semantics)
- `phase2_frac: 0.1`, `val_frac: 0.1`, batch 2048, patience 5

```bash
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/ablations/03_shap_plus_huim/run.py
```

## Results

| Model | AUC | ACC | ΔAUC vs baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| MLP | 0.5690 | 0.5957 | **+0.0162** |
| AutoInt | 0.5705 | 0.6021 | −0.0121 |
| ResNet | 0.5534 | 0.5934 | **+0.0169** |

**Finding:** the proposed method helps MLP (+1.6 AUC pts) and ResNet (+1.7 pts) while using 10 original features instead of 19 — but it *loses* 1.2 pts on AutoInt, the baseline's best model, so the best overall AUC drops from 0.5826 to 0.5705. Accuracy is up on all three. The headline claim ("SHAP+HUIM adds 1–2% AUC") holds per-architecture for MLP/ResNet, not for the best model. FTTransformer was not run in this arm.

children.title: 04 HUIM-only — mined patterns, no raw features
children.summary: Drop every original column; the 40 binary HUIM pattern columns are the entire input
children.notes:
## Setup

- `features.mode: huim_only`, `exclude_cols: []`, `top_drivers_n: 20`, `top_protectors_n: 20`, `n_bins: 5`
- Reads patterns directly from `../../shap_huim_extractions/01_2024_baseline/csvs/` (unlike 02/03, which expect the copied `SHAP_HUIM/` dir)
- Best hyperparameters found (`best_params.json`): MLP `d_model 128, n_layers 10, lr 1e-3`; ResNet `d_model 128, n_layers 10, lr 1e-5`

```bash
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/ablations/04_huim_only/run.py
```

## Results

| Model | AUC | ACC |
|---|---|---|
| MLP | 0.5234 | 0.5801 |
| AutoInt | 0.5174 | 0.5802 |
| ResNet | 0.5213 | 0.5797 |

**Finding:** patterns alone are barely above chance (AUC 0.517–0.523) and accuracy collapses to roughly the majority-class rate (~0.58) — the models are close to predicting a single class. Confirms the mined itemsets are a *complement*, not a substitute: they carry combinatorial context but discard the individual feature effects that do the real work in 01/03.

children.title: 05 LLM-Select feature scoring (no model trained)
children.summary: Rank all 19 features with a local LLM (LLM-Score) and compare that ranking against SHAP and HUIM
children.notes:
## Setup

- Method: **LLM-Score** from *LLM-Select: Feature Selection with Large Language Models* (Jeong, Lipton & Ravikumar, TMLR 2025)
- Model: local Ollama **qwen2.5:7b**, importance in [0,1] per feature, **3 repeats** each, aggregated as mean ± std
- Two prompt variants: `data_free` (feature name + description + task context only — paper-faithful) and `data_informed` (same plus 100 sample rows from `output/llm_sample_raw.csv`, with raw `ARR_DELAY` dropped so the target does not leak)
- Audit trail: one JSON per feature per repeat under `output/raw_llm_outputs/<variant>/`

```bash
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/ablations/05_baseline_100_data/run.py
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/ablations/05_baseline_100_data/compare.py
```

## Findings

- The LLM and SHAP **disagree sharply**. SHAP's #1 feature `O_LONGITUDE` (mean|SHAP| 0.110, ~1.7× the next) is scored *near the bottom* by the LLM (0.23 data-free / 0.17 data-informed) — the LLM reads longitude as "a rough proxy with limited direct predictive power", while SHAP finds it is the model's Northeast-US delay signal.
- Conversely the LLM's #1, `ORIGIN_INDEX` (0.80), is only SHAP rank 10, and it rates weather (`O_PRCP` 0.77, `O_WSPD` 0.75) far above SHAP ranks 12–13.
- The LLM ranks on **plausible causal stories**; SHAP ranks on **what this model actually used**. Showing the LLM 100 sample rows barely moves it — data-free and data-informed pick the identical top-10 set and only reorder within it; they diverge only at top-5, where they share just `ORIGIN_INDEX` and `O_PRCP`.

No model is trained in this arm — it only produces the ranking CSVs consumed by the 06_* arms, plus `comparison.csv`, `comparison_report.md` and three figures.

children.title: 06 LLM top-10 features
children.summary: Train on the 10 highest LLM-scored features — the direct counterpart to the (unrun) SHAP-only arm
children.notes:
## Setup

- `features.mode: llm_only`, `top_n: 10`, ranking from `05_baseline_100_data/output/llm_feature_importance_datafree.csv`
- Training config mirrors 02/03 exactly (`phase2_frac 0.1`, `val_frac 0.1`, batch 2048, patience 5) so the arms are comparable
- At top-10 the data-free and data-informed prompts select the **identical** set (they differ only in ordering), so this one arm covers both variants

```bash
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/ablations/06_llm_top10/run.py
```

## Results

| Model | AUC | ACC | ΔAUC vs baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| MLP | 0.5182 | 0.5764 | −0.0345 |
| AutoInt | 0.5728 | **0.6061** | −0.0098 |
| ResNet | 0.5153 | 0.5762 | −0.0212 |

**Finding:** a 7B model ranking features from their *names alone* gets AutoInt to 0.5728 AUC and the best accuracy of any arm (0.6061) — respectable for zero data access. But MLP and ResNet fall to near-chance (0.515–0.518), and every model trails the SHAP+HUIM arm. The LLM's set survives only in the architecture that models feature interactions itself.

children.title: 06_1 LLM top-5, data-free prompt
children.summary: Tighten to 5 features using the paper-faithful prompt (names + descriptions + task only)
children.notes:
## Setup

- `top_n: 5` from `llm_feature_importance_datafree.csv` — selects `ORIGIN_INDEX, O_PRCP, O_WSPD, OP_CARRIER, CRS_DEP_TIME_MIN`
- Paired with 06_2 to test whether showing the LLM 100 sample rows changes *which* features it picks well. Top-5 is the cut where the two variants diverge.

```bash
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/ablations/06_1_llm_top5_datafree/run.py
```

## Results

| Model | AUC | ACC |
|---|---|---|
| MLP | 0.5000 | 0.5763 |
| AutoInt | 0.5552 | 0.5949 |
| ResNet | 0.5000 | 0.5763 |

**Finding:** the floor. MLP and ResNet land at **exactly 0.5000 AUC** with accuracy pinned at the positive-class rate — they have degenerated to constant predictors; 5 name-picked features carry no usable signal for them. AutoInt still extracts 0.5552. Cutting 10 → 5 costs AutoInt 1.8 AUC pts.

children.title: 06_2 LLM top-5, data-informed prompt
children.summary: Same 5-feature budget, but the LLM saw 100 sample rows before scoring
children.notes:
## Setup

- `top_n: 5` from `llm_feature_importance_datainformed.csv` — selects `CRS_ELAPSED_TIME, ORIGIN_INDEX, CRS_ARR_TIME_MIN, O_PRCP, FL_WEEK`
- Shares only `ORIGIN_INDEX` and `O_PRCP` with 06_1; identical training config, so the only difference is the prompt variant

```bash
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/ablations/06_2_llm_top5_datainformed/run.py
```

## Results

| Model | AUC | ACC | vs 06_1 (data-free) |
|---|---|---|---|
| MLP | 0.5019 | 0.5770 | +0.0019 |
| AutoInt | 0.5502 | 0.5907 | −0.0050 |
| ResNet | 0.5062 | 0.5771 | +0.0062 |

**Finding:** **showing the LLM the data does not help.** Despite picking a largely different 5-feature set, results land within ~0.5 AUC pts of the data-free variant in both directions (AutoInt slightly worse, MLP/ResNet marginally better but still at chance). Combined with the top-10 result — where both prompts choose the *identical* set — the 100 sample rows change the LLM's stated reasoning far more than its actual selection quality.

title: Representation bake-off — one fixed MLP head
summary: Controlled comparison of tabular representations feeding an identical classifier head; only the input embedding varies
notes:
## Setup (identical across every row)

- 50k rows stratified over **all years 2016–2024** (only 2020 and 2024 shipped pre-processed; the other 7 were generated by `prep/build_tab_years.py`), temporal `FL_DAY` split — train 14,690 / val 4,985 / test 30,325
- Target `|ARR_DELAY| > 15` (40.8% positive)
- One plain-torch MLP head (`[256,128]`, dropout 0.1, Adam 1e-3, batch 2048, early stop on val AUC) — deliberately **not** mambular's MLPClassifier, which would re-embed raw columns and confound the comparison
- AUC primary, plus F1-macro and accuracy, mean ± std over seeds `[42, 43, 44]`

```bash
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/representation_bakeoff/prep/build_tab_years.py
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/representation_bakeoff/prep/build_sample.py
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/representation_bakeoff/run_bakeoff.py
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/representation_bakeoff/huim/mine.py
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/representation_bakeoff/run_hybrid.py
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/representation_bakeoff/make_figures.py
```

**Finding:** representation choice moves AUC by ~2.6 pts, and the ceiling stays ~0.60 AUC regardless — consistent with the 2020 ablations above. This root is the shared harness; the arms below are the four representations.

children.title: A — SentenceTransformer (MiniLM)
children.summary: Serialize each row to "col=value; …" text and embed with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-d)
children.notes:
## Setup

- `embeddings/embed_sentence_transformer.py`, model `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, no fitting (frozen encoder, downloads on first run)

**Finding:** the **weakest** representation and the noisiest (AUC std 0.0042, ~3× skrub's; F1 std 0.041). As expected — serialising rows to text lets the tokenizer mangle the numeric features, and it needs 384 dimensions to underperform a 95-d matrix.

children.title: B — skrub TableVectorizer
children.summary: TableVectorizer fit on train only → bounded 95-d numeric matrix (bake-off winner)
children.notes:
## Setup

- `embeddings/embed_skrub.py`, `cardinality_threshold: 40`, StandardScaler after; fit on the train split only

**Finding:** **the winner**, by a clear low-variance margin — +2.6 AUC pts over SentenceTransformer at a quarter of the dimensionality (95-d vs 384-d), with the tightest seed spread of any arm (±0.0014). It also produces the most compact, interpretable matrix. Best F1-macro (0.537) and best accuracy (0.600) in the bake-off.

children.title: D — skrub + HUIM delay-cost patterns
children.summary: Concatenate 40 binary HUIM pattern columns onto the winning skrub embedding
children.notes:
## Setup

- `huim/mine.py` then `run_hybrid.py` (auto-picks the winner from `results.csv`)
- **Utility had to be synthesised** — flight data has no natural utility column: each item in a **delayed** flight carries that flight's `|ARR_DELAY|` (delay cost); in an **on-time** flight it carries the on-time margin `(15 − |ARR_DELAY|)`
- Mined per class with PAMI EFIM on **train rows only**: minUtil p98, patterns ≤ 3 items, top-200 kept, 20 drivers + 20 protectors used. `OP_CARRIER_FL_NUM` excluded as an item (thousands of singletons → combinatorial blow-up)

**Finding:** **HUIM does not help here — reported as-is, with no tuning toward a positive result.** Adding 40 pattern columns *lowered* AUC by 0.6 pts (0.5919 vs 0.5982), a real negative outside the seed-noise band (3.5σ of the seed-to-seed difference), not a wash; F1-macro is down a marginal 1.1σ and accuracy is within noise. On this data the mined patterns add nothing skrub does not already encode.

Top mined delay driver: `CRS_DEP_TIME_MIN=VeryLow + D_LATITUDE=VeryHigh`.

Note this **contradicts** ablation 03 on the 2020 data, where the same idea gained 1.6–1.7 AUC pts for MLP/ResNet. The difference: there HUIM patterns were added to a *reduced* 10-feature SHAP set, here to an already-rich 95-d learned encoding — supporting the reading that HUIM supplies context a weak feature set lacks, and is redundant once the representation is strong.

children.title: C — TabPFN frozen embedder
children.summary: TabPFN as a frozen feature extractor into the same head — built but never evaluated
children.notes:
## Setup

- `embeddings/embed_tabpfn.py` is **written and ready**: context cap 10,000 rows, batch 4,096, `n_estimators: 2` averaged into the embedding
- `run_bakeoff.py` wraps each representation in try/except, so this arm failing did not sink A and B

**Blocked:** `tabpfn 8.x` (Prior Labs) gates the model weights behind a one-time license/token, so no weights were available at run time. No numbers exist for this row.

**To unblock:** create a free Prior Labs account, accept the license, then

```bash
export TABPFN_TOKEN=<key>
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/representation_bakeoff/run_bakeoff.py --only tabpfn
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/representation_bakeoff/run_hybrid.py --winner <best>
```

title: SHAP × HUIM extraction — 2024 baseline
summary: Upstream pattern-mining run that produces the driver/protector CSVs every SHAP+HUIM ablation consumes
notes:
## Setup

- Data: `Flight_tab_2024.csv`, `sample_frac: 0.1` of train (~600K → ~60K rows), same temporal `FL_DAY` split
- Train an MLP binary classifier, then SHAP `KernelExplainer` with `bg_samples: 200`, `test_samples: 1000` → a (1000 × n_features) SHAP matrix
- Discretise continuous features with `KBinsDiscretizer` (5 quantile bins, **fit on train only**) → categorical items
- Split into two transaction streams: **positive SHAP = delay drivers**, **negative SHAP = delay protectors**. Utility = `int(|SHAP| × 10000)` (`shap_scale` avoids integer-rounding loss in PAMI)
- Mine each stream with **PAMI EFIM**, `minUtil` = 90th percentile of transaction utilities

```bash
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/shap_huim_extractions/01_2024_baseline/run.py
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/shap_huim_extractions/01_2024_baseline/visualize.py
```

## Findings

1. **Geography is the strongest signal** — `O_LONGITUDE=VeryHigh` (Northeast US) has utility 540K and appears in nearly every top driver pattern; `O_LATITUDE=High + O_LONGITUDE=VeryHigh` (NYC area) is 463K.
2. **Weather amplifies only in combination** — wind/temperature alone are moderate, but `CRS_ELAPSED_TIME=VeryHigh + O_WSPD=VeryHigh + O_LONGITUDE=VeryHigh` reaches 96K.
3. **Carrier-specific effects** — DL/AA at Northeast airports drive delay; WN/OO on short regional routes protect against it.
4. **Asymmetry:** ~7× more protector patterns (69,061) than driver patterns (9,565) — on-time performance has diffuse causes, delays are driven by fewer concentrated factors.
5. Top patterns are 2–4 features — specific enough to act on, general enough to cover many flights.

⚠️ **Hand-off gotcha:** ablations 02/03 read `../../SHAP_HUIM/{shap_feature_importance,huim_delay_drivers,huim_delay_protectors}.csv`, but this script writes to its own local `csvs/`. That `SHAP_HUIM/` directory **does not currently exist** — outputs must be copied there before 02/03 can run. Ablation 04 sidesteps this by pointing straight at `csvs/`.

children.title: v2 — wider SHAP sample, looser minUtil
children.summary: Re-run the extraction with 2× the sample, 2× background/test instances, and minUtil at p80 instead of p90
children.notes:
## Setup — the only four knobs changed

| Parameter | baseline | v2 |
|---|---|---|
| `sample_frac` | 0.1 | **0.2** |
| `bg_samples` | 200 | **400** |
| `test_samples` | 1000 | **2000** |
| `min_util_percentile` | 90 | **80** |

Everything else (year, split, `n_bins: 5`, `shap_scale: 10000`) is unchanged.

```bash
uv run python exp/Tab_exp/shap_huim_extractions/01_2024_v2/run.py
```

## Findings

- **Pattern count explodes:** drivers 9,565 → **368,777** (39×), protectors 69,061 → **503,731** (7×). Dropping minUtil from p90 to p80 dominates this; the driver stream is far more sensitive because its utility distribution is more concentrated.
- **The SHAP ranking is not stable across sample size.** `O_LONGITUDE` stays #1 (0.110 → 0.100), but ranks 2–4 reshuffle: `CRS_DEP_TIME_MIN` jumps from rank 6 to **rank 3** (0.044 → 0.061, +38%) while `OP_CARRIER` falls from rank 2 to 4 (0.065 → 0.052) and `O_TEMP` leaves the top 4. With only 1,000 explained instances the baseline ranking carries real sampling noise — worth flagging, since `top_shap_n: 10` in arms 02/03 is cut from exactly that ranking.
- **Not yet consumed downstream:** every ablation still points at `01_2024_baseline/csvs/`. Also the driver/protector asymmetry flips character here (1.4× rather than 7×), so the baseline's "7× more protectors" finding is partly a threshold artifact rather than a property of the data.
